title: egymás: Saying What People Do To or With Each Other

sections.title: A pronoun that always needs a case ending
sections.content: egymás means "each other"/"one another" and describes an action that goes both ways between two or more people. It never appears bare as a subject or object — like the reflexive magam/magad/magát you already know, it always carries whatever case ending the verb governs. The trick is the same one you use for any object: first decide what case the verb needs, then put that case ending on egymás, not on the verb itself.

sections.title: Matching the case to the verb

items.english: We talk a lot with each other.

sections.content: Ask yourself what case the verb would need for any ordinary object, then attach that same case to egymás: szeret takes an accusative object, so szeretjük egymást; segít takes a dative object, so segítünk egymásnak; beszélget takes -val/-vel, so beszélgetünk egymással. egymással assimilates the -val exactly like any noun ending in -s (ház + val → házzal, egymás + val → egymással).
